# jenkins_node_secret (Data Source)

Get the connection secret of an inbound (JNLP) agent node, as passed to `agent.jar -secret`. Requires the Agent/Connect permission on the node.

The secret is marked sensitive but is stored in plain text in the Terraform state; secure the state backend accordingly.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "jenkins_node" "agent" {
  name      = "linux-agent-01"
  remote_fs = "/home/jenkins/agent"
}

# Referencing the node's id defers the lookup until the node exists.
data "jenkins_node_secret" "agent" {
  name = jenkins_node.agent.id
}

# Pass data.jenkins_node_secret.agent.secret to the agent, e.g.
# java -jar agent.jar -url <jenkins-url> -name linux-agent-01 -secret <secret>
```

~> The secret is read from `/computer/<name>/jenkins-agent.jnlp`, an endpoint Jenkins has deprecated. The controller logs a WARNING every time it is fetched, so each plan or apply emits one such line per `jenkins_node_secret`. Jenkins has no supported replacement yet; this data source will switch to it once one ships.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the agent node.

### Read-Only

- `secret` (String, Sensitive) The inbound agent connection secret.
